questions.title: Aqueous humour is secreted by:
questions.question: Aqueous humour is secreted by:

explanations.A: The anterior chamber angle is the site of aqueous drainage via the trabecular meshwork, not its site of secretion.
explanations.B: Aqueous humour is secreted by the ciliary body, specifically the non-pigmented epithelium of its pars plicata, into the posterior chamber. From there it flows through the pupil into the anterior chamber before draining at the angle. This secretory role is what maintains normal intraocular pressure and nourishes the avascular cornea and lens.
explanations.C: The posterior iris surface is not a secretory structure for aqueous humour; the ciliary body immediately behind it is.
explanations.D: The lens has no secretory function; it is a refractive structure suspended by the zonules, not a source of aqueous humour.

questions.title: Aqueous humor is drained through:
questions.question: Aqueous humor is drained through:

explanations.A: Aqueous humour drains through the anterior chamber angle, where the trabecular meshwork channels it into Schlemm's canal and onward into the episcleral venous system. This drainage pathway regulates intraocular pressure, since production and drainage must balance for pressure to stay normal. Obstruction along this route, most classically at the trabecular meshwork, is the basis of glaucoma.
explanations.B: The ciliary body is where aqueous humour is produced, not where it drains.
explanations.C: The posterior iris surface plays no role in aqueous drainage; it lies upstream, near the site of secretion.
explanations.D: The lens is not part of the drainage pathway; aqueous flows around it, not through it.

questions.title: Aqueous humour is produced in which chamber of the eye:
questions.question: Aqueous humour is produced in which chamber of the eye:

explanations.A: Aqueous humour is produced in the posterior, not the anterior, chamber; it only reaches the anterior chamber after flowing through the pupil.
explanations.B: Aqueous humour is produced in the posterior chamber, behind the iris and in front of the lens and its zonules, by the ciliary body's non-pigmented epithelium. It then passes forward through the pupil into the anterior chamber, where it eventually drains at the angle. Because the posterior, not the anterior, chamber is the true production site, confusing the two is a common source of error.
explanations.C: The vitreous cavity is filled with vitreous gel, not aqueous humour, and plays no part in aqueous production.
explanations.D: The trabecular meshwork is a drainage structure at the angle, not a site of aqueous production.

questions.title: The outer coat of the eye:
questions.question: The outer coat of the eye:

options.A: Formed of cornea, sclera and iris.
options.C: Cornea does not have refractive function.
options.D: Protects against the invasion of micro-organisms.

explanations.A: The outer coat is formed of the cornea and sclera only; the iris belongs to the middle (uveal), not the outer, coat.
explanations.B: The outer coat is not only protective — the cornea, its anterior part, also provides the eye's principal refractive power.
explanations.C: The cornea does have refractive function; it contributes the larger share of the eye's total refractive power, more than the lens.
explanations.D: The outer fibrous coat — cornea anteriorly, sclera posteriorly — forms a tough protective shell around the eye's contents. Beyond its mechanical role, it acts as a barrier against the invasion of micro-organisms, helping keep the eye's interior sterile. This protective function is distinct from, and in addition to, the cornea's separate optical role in refraction.

questions.title: The middle coat of the eye:
questions.question: The middle coat of the eye:

options.C: Consists of the iris, ciliary body and retina.
options.D: Is also called the neurosensory coat.

explanations.A: The uveal tract — iris, ciliary body and choroid — forms the eye's middle coat and is also known as the vascular coat because of its rich blood supply, which nourishes adjacent structures. It commonly carries pigment, but 'vascular coat' is the description this bank's key affirms as correct here. This vascularity distinguishes the uvea from the avascular cornea and lens, and from the outer fibrous coat.
explanations.B: While the uveal tract may indeed be pigmented, that is not the property this question's key selects as correct — 'the vascular coat' description is.
explanations.C: The middle coat is the iris, ciliary body and choroid, not the retina — the retina belongs to the innermost, neurosensory coat, a separate layer.
explanations.D: 'Neurosensory coat' refers to the retina, the innermost layer, not the vascular middle coat that this question concerns.

questions.title: Nasolacrimal duct opens in:
questions.question: Nasolacrimal duct opens in:

explanations.A: Tears drain into the inferior, not the superior, nasal meatus.
explanations.B: The nasolacrimal duct carries tears from the lacrimal sac down into the nose, opening into the inferior meatus, beneath the inferior nasal concha. This detail matters clinically because obstruction anywhere along this pathway — from the punctum through the canaliculi, sac and duct to this opening — causes epiphora and predisposes to dacryocystitis. The duct's course runs within the lateral wall of the nose, ending specifically at this inferior point.
explanations.C: The duct opens into the inferior, not the middle, nasal meatus.
explanations.D: The nasopharynx is not where the nasolacrimal duct opens; it opens into the nasal cavity itself, at the inferior meatus.

questions.title: The cornea is covered by:
questions.question: The cornea is covered by:

explanations.A: Keratinised epithelium covers the skin, not the cornea; a keratinised corneal surface would be opaque and incompatible with clear vision.
explanations.B: The corneal surface is covered by non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium, continuous at the limbus with the conjunctival epithelium. Being non-keratinised keeps the surface smooth, transparent, and able to stay adequately hydrated by the tear film, which the eye's optical function depends on. This is one of several features, alongside avascularity and regular stromal collagen spacing, that keep the cornea transparent.
explanations.C: Pseudo-stratified columnar epithelium lines structures such as the respiratory tract, not the cornea.
explanations.D: Stratified columnar epithelium is not the corneal epithelial type; the cornea's epithelium is stratified squamous, non-keratinised specifically.

questions.title: corneal transparency is due to all of the following factors EXCEPT:
questions.question: corneal transparency is due to all of the following factors EXCEPT:

options.A: compact arrangement of corneal stromal fibers

explanations.A: Compact, regular arrangement of the stromal collagen fibres is a genuine transparency factor, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Avascularity (lack of blood vessels) is a genuine corneal transparency factor, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: The cornea's sensory nerve fibres, making it one of the most densely innervated tissues in the body, are unmyelinated within the stroma and epithelium — myelination only begins more peripherally, near the limbus. Myelinated fibres running through the central cornea would scatter light and disrupt transparency, so the cornea's nerve supply is specifically non-myelinated as a transparency-preserving feature. This is why 'myelinated nerve fibres' is the false statement among genuine transparency factors such as avascularity, epithelial non-keratinisation, and regular stromal collagen spacing.
explanations.D: Non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium is a genuine transparency factor, so it is not the exception.

questions.title: The cornea has:
questions.question: The cornea has:

explanations.A: The cornea has five histological layers (epithelium, Bowman's, stroma, Descemet's, endothelium), not three.
explanations.B: The cornea is avascular, not richly vascularised; rich vasculature would in fact impair, not support, its transparency.
explanations.C: The corneal endothelium maintains the stroma's relative dehydration through active Na+/K+-ATPase ion pumps, continuously pumping fluid out of the stroma against the cornea's tendency to imbibe water. This active endothelial pump function is essential for corneal transparency: stromal oedema from pump failure clouds the cornea. It is this active, energy-dependent pumping, not passive properties like vascularity or fibre arrangement, that this question's key identifies as the defining feature here.
explanations.D: The stromal collagen fibrils are regularly, not irregularly, arranged in parallel lamellae; irregular arrangement would scatter light and impair transparency.
explanations.E: The cornea in fact maintains relative dehydration, not rich water content; excess water content (oedema) would impair, not support, transparency.

questions.title: The refractive power of the eye lens is about… in diopters:
questions.question: The refractive power of the eye lens is about… in diopters:

explanations.A: 10 dioptres understates the lens's typical relaxed refractive contribution, which is closer to 20.
explanations.B: The relaxed crystalline lens contributes roughly 20 dioptres to the eye's total refractive power of about 60 dioptres, with the cornea supplying the larger remaining share. This division of labour between cornea (fixed, larger contribution) and lens (variable, smaller contribution, able to increase with accommodation) lets the eye focus on both distant and near objects. The lens's own power can rise further during accommodation as the ciliary muscle contracts and the lens rounds up.
explanations.C: 30 dioptres overstates the lens's typical relaxed contribution; that figure is closer to the cornea's own share.
explanations.D: 40 dioptres is closer to the cornea's refractive contribution, not the lens's, which is roughly half that.

questions.title: The cornea is made of the following layers EXCEPT:
questions.question: The cornea is made of the following layers EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Bowman's membrane is a genuine corneal layer, lying just beneath the epithelium, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: The corneal stroma is a genuine corneal layer — indeed the thickest one — so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Bruch's membrane is not a layer of the cornea at all: it is a distinct structure within the choroid, separating the retinal pigment epithelium from the choroidal capillaries at the back of the eye. The cornea's own layers are the epithelium, Bowman's layer, the stroma, Descemet's membrane and the endothelium. Because Bruch's membrane belongs to an entirely different part of the eye, it is the one option here that is not a corneal layer.
explanations.D: The endothelium is a genuine corneal layer, its innermost one, so it is not the exception.

questions.title: Factors affecting the corneal transparency include the following EXCEPT:
questions.question: Factors affecting the corneal transparency include the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Corneal avascularity is a genuine transparency factor, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: The endothelial pump is a genuine transparency factor, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Regular arrangement of the stromal lamellae is a genuine transparency factor, so it is not the exception.
explanations.D: A keratinised epithelium is not one of the cornea's transparency factors — quite the opposite. The cornea's actual epithelium is non-keratinised, which is itself part of what keeps the surface smooth and transparent; keratinisation, the process that makes skin opaque and protective, would cloud the corneal surface. This is why keratinised epithelium is the exception among genuine transparency factors such as avascularity, the endothelial pump and regular stromal collagen arrangement.

questions.title: The uveal tract is composed of the following EXCEPT:
questions.question: The uveal tract is composed of the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: The iris is a genuine component of the uveal tract, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: The ciliary body is a genuine component of the uveal tract, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: The uveal tract is composed of the iris, ciliary body and choroid — collectively the eye's vascular middle coat. The retina is a separate structure entirely: the innermost, neurosensory coat, developmentally and anatomically distinct from the uvea. Because the retina is never one of the uveal tract's own components, it is the exception among these four options.
explanations.D: The choroid is a genuine component of the uveal tract, so it is not the exception.

questions.title: The posterior chamber is the space between:
questions.question: The posterior chamber is the space between:

options.A: The crystalline lens and the iris.
options.B: The crystalline lens and the vitreous.
options.D: The ciliary body and the crystalline lens.

explanations.A: The posterior chamber is the narrow space bounded anteriorly by the posterior surface of the iris and posteriorly by the crystalline lens (with its zonular fibres), lying behind the iris and in front of the lens. This is the simplified boundary pair most texts use to describe the chamber, distinguishing it from the anterior chamber (between the iris and the cornea) on the other side of the iris. The ciliary body also borders the chamber peripherally, but the iris and the lens are its two defining anterior/posterior boundaries.
explanations.B: The lens and the vitreous meet at the exit of the posterior chamber into the vitreous cavity, but that is not the boundary pair this key selects.
explanations.C: The iris and the cornea bound the anterior, not the posterior, chamber.
explanations.D: The ciliary body borders the posterior chamber peripherally, and the lens is one of its true boundaries, but this key specifically selects the iris/lens boundary pair, not the ciliary-body/lens pair.

questions.title: The conjunctiva is formed of the following parts EXCEPT:
questions.question: The conjunctiva is formed of the following parts EXCEPT:

explanations.A: The palpebral part is a genuine conjunctival division, lining the inner eyelid, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: The bulbar part is a genuine conjunctival division, covering the anterior sclera, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: The fornices are genuine conjunctival divisions, where the palpebral and bulbar parts reflect into each other, so they are not the exception.
explanations.D: The tarsus is not a part of the conjunctiva — it is the dense fibrous connective-tissue plate that gives the eyelid its shape and structural rigidity, lying deep to the palpebral conjunctiva rather than being part of the conjunctival membrane itself. The conjunctiva's own three continuous parts are the palpebral conjunctiva, the bulbar conjunctiva, and the fornices. Because the tarsus is a different tissue layer entirely, it is the one option here that is not a conjunctival part.

questions.title: The following is an investigation not a part of the ophthalmic examination:
questions.question: The following is an investigation not a part of the ophthalmic examination:

explanations.A: Autorefractometry is a routine part of the ophthalmic examination, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Indirect ophthalmoscopy is a routine part of fundus examination, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Optical coherence tomography is a specialised cross-sectional imaging investigation, reserved for specific indications such as macular or optic-nerve disease, rather than a component performed as part of every routine ophthalmic examination. The routine examination itself centres on visual acuity, pupillary reflexes, slit-lamp assessment, tonometry, autorefractometry and ophthalmoscopy. Because OCT sits outside that routine set, per this bank's key, it is the exception here.
explanations.D: Tonometry (intraocular pressure measurement) is a routine part of the ophthalmic examination, so it is not the exception.

questions.title: One of the following statements is false:
questions.question: One of the following statements is false:

options.A: A white reflex may indicate mature cataract.
options.C: A black reflex is seen in vitreous haemorrhage.
options.D: A yellow reflex points to endophthalmitis.

explanations.A: A white (leukocoric) reflex genuinely can indicate mature cataract, so this statement is true, not the false one asked for.
explanations.B: There is no recognised 'blue' red-reflex finding associated with glaucoma. Glaucoma is instead diagnosed from raised intraocular pressure, optic disc cupping and visual field loss — none of which produce a distinctive reflex colour change of the kind a white, black or yellow reflex represents for cataract, vitreous haemorrhage or endophthalmitis. Because this pairing of 'blue reflex' with glaucoma does not correspond to any real clinical sign, it is the false statement among the four.
explanations.C: A black reflex genuinely can be seen in dense vitreous haemorrhage, so this statement is true, not the false one asked for.
explanations.D: A yellow reflex genuinely can point to endophthalmitis, so this statement is true, not the false one asked for.

questions.title: The orbit:
questions.question: The orbit:

options.A: The orbit is a 3- walled cone.
options.B: The orbit is closely related to paranasal sinuses.
options.C: The orbit communicates with the skull via 4 main ports.
options.D: The commonest cause of orbital cellulitis is conjunctivitis.

explanations.A: The orbit is a four-walled, not three-walled, pyramidal structure (roof, floor, medial and lateral walls), so this statement is false.
explanations.B: The bony orbit is closely related to the surrounding paranasal sinuses on three of its four walls: the roof borders the frontal sinus, the floor borders the maxillary sinus, and the medial wall borders the ethmoid sinus. This close relationship is clinically important, since sinus disease can spread into the orbit through these thin bony walls. It is this genuine anatomical closeness, not a false claim, that makes this the true statement among the four.
explanations.C: The orbit communicates with adjacent spaces through several named canals and fissures (optic canal, superior and inferior orbital fissures, and smaller foramina), not a settled count of '4 main ports', so this statement is not the one the key affirms.
explanations.D: The commonest cause of orbital cellulitis is spread from sinusitis (particularly ethmoiditis), not simple conjunctivitis, so this statement is false.

questions.title: Regarding the anatomy of the cornea:
questions.question: Regarding the anatomy of the cornea:

options.A: Cornea is made up of 7 layers.
options.B: The stroma is made of collagen fibers arranged in lamellae.
options.C: Corneal transparency is due to vascularity.
options.D: Active endothelial pump plays a minor role in transparency of cornea.

explanations.A: The cornea has five histological layers (epithelium, Bowman's, stroma, Descemet's, endothelium), not seven, so this statement is false.
explanations.B: The corneal stroma, the cornea's thickest layer, is made of collagen fibrils arranged in regularly spaced parallel lamellae. This precise, near-crystalline regularity of spacing, not the mere presence of collagen, is what allows destructive light-scattering interference between adjacent fibrils to cancel out, keeping the stroma transparent. It is this genuine structural fact, among several false statements about corneal anatomy, that the key affirms here.
explanations.C: Corneal transparency is due to avascularity, not vascularity — blood vessels in the cornea would scatter light and cause opacity, which is why corneal vascularisation is a pathological finding.
explanations.D: The active endothelial pump plays a major, not minor, role in transparency, continuously removing fluid to keep the stroma relatively dehydrated.

questions.title: If the corneal light reflex is 2mm temporal to the pupil in the right eye, the deviation is estimated to be:
questions.question: If the corneal light reflex is 2mm temporal to the pupil in the right eye, the deviation is estimated to be:

explanations.A: 10 dioptres corresponds to about 1mm of reflex decentration, not the 2mm described here.
explanations.B: 20 dioptres would correspond to roughly 1.3mm of decentration on the working Hirschberg estimate, not the full 2mm described here.
explanations.C: The Hirschberg test estimates the angle of manifest strabismus from how far the corneal light reflex is displaced from the pupil centre, using the working estimate that each millimetre of decentration corresponds to roughly 15 dioptres of deviation. A reflex displaced 2mm temporal to the pupil in the right eye is consistent with the eye being turned inward (esotropia), and 2mm at ~15 dioptres/mm works out to about 30 dioptres. This bedside estimate lets a clinician quantify a squint without needing a prism bar.
explanations.D: 40 dioptres would correspond to a decentration greater than the 2mm described in this scenario.

questions.title: Methods of fundus examination include the following EXCEPT:
questions.question: Methods of fundus examination include the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy with an accessory fundus lens is a genuine fundus-examination method, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: Direct ophthalmoscopy is a genuine fundus-examination method, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: Indirect ophthalmoscopy is a genuine fundus-examination method, so it is not the exception.
explanations.D: Retinoscopy is not a fundus-examination method — despite using a similarly styled instrument and observing a light reflex from the eye, its purpose is entirely different: it objectively measures the eye's refractive error by observing how the retinoscopic reflex moves as lenses are interposed, rather than examining the retina's structure. Genuine fundus-examination methods are direct and indirect ophthalmoscopy and slit-lamp biomicroscopy with a fundus lens. Because retinoscopy serves a refractive, not a fundus-examination, purpose, it is the exception among these four.

questions.title: Visual field-testing using confrontation method can diagnose:
questions.question: Visual field-testing using confrontation method can diagnose:

explanations.A: An enlarged blind spot is too small and localised a defect for the coarse resolution of confrontation testing to reliably detect.
explanations.B: A paracentral scotoma is too small and localised a defect for confrontation testing's coarse resolution to reliably detect.
explanations.C: Confrontation visual field testing, comparing the patient's field to the examiner's own quadrant by quadrant, is a quick bedside screening method. Its resolution is coarse, but it is well suited to detecting a large field defect such as a hemianopia — loss of an entire half of the visual field, typically from a lesion affecting the optic tract or radiations behind the chiasm. Smaller, more localised defects such as a paracentral scotoma or a subtle nasal step generally need formal, more sensitive perimetry to detect reliably.
explanations.D: A subtle nasal step is too small a defect for confrontation testing's coarse resolution to reliably detect.

questions.title: Regarding the paranasal sinuses the following is true EXCEPT:
questions.question: Regarding the paranasal sinuses the following is true EXCEPT:

options.A: The ethmoid sinus is located medially.
options.B: The roof of the orbit separates the orbit from the frontal sinus.
options.C: The lateral wall separates the orbit from the sphenoid sinus.
options.D: The floor separates the orbit from the maxillary sinus.

explanations.A: The ethmoid sinus genuinely lies medial to the orbit, so this statement is true, not the exception.
explanations.B: The orbital roof genuinely separates the orbit from the frontal sinus above it, so this statement is true, not the exception.
explanations.C: The orbit's lateral wall borders the temporal fossa, not the sphenoid sinus — the sphenoid sinus instead lies posterior to the orbital apex, related to the back of the orbit rather than its lateral wall. The orbit's genuine sinus relationships are the frontal sinus (roof), the ethmoid sinus (medial wall) and the maxillary sinus (floor). Because the lateral wall's stated relation to the sphenoid sinus does not hold, this is the false statement among the four.
explanations.D: The orbital floor genuinely separates the orbit from the maxillary sinus below it, so this statement is true, not the exception.

questions.title: The crystalline lens is suspended from ciliary body processes by:
questions.question: The crystalline lens is suspended from ciliary body processes by:

explanations.A: 'Sutures' refers to the internal lines where lens fibres meet within the lens substance, not to the suspensory mechanism.
explanations.B: The crystalline lens is suspended in position by the zonule of Zinn — a ring of fine fibres running from the ciliary body's processes to the lens capsule's equator. Zonular tension at rest flattens the lens for distance focus; when the ciliary muscle contracts during accommodation, zonular tension relaxes and the lens rounds up to increase its refractive power for near vision. This suspension keeps the lens centred on the visual axis between the iris and the vitreous.
explanations.C: The lens capsule is the lens's own outer covering, not the structure that suspends it from the ciliary body.
explanations.D: Lens fibres are the lens's own internal cellular structure, not the suspensory apparatus that holds the lens in place.

questions.title: The following is not a structure of anterior chamber angle:
questions.question: The following is not a structure of anterior chamber angle:

explanations.A: The trabecular meshwork is a genuine structure of the anterior chamber angle, so it is not the exception.
explanations.B: The scleral spur is a genuine structure of the anterior chamber angle, forming its posterior landmark, so it is not the exception.
explanations.C: The retinal pigment epithelium is a layer of the retina, at the back of the eye — it has no anatomical place in the anterior chamber angle at the front. The angle's own genuine structures are the trabecular meshwork (the drainage filter), Schwalbe's line (the peripheral end of Descemet's membrane) and the scleral spur (the posterior boundary). Because the retinal pigment epithelium belongs to an entirely different part of the eye, it is the one option here that is not a structure of the angle.
explanations.D: Schwalbe's line is a genuine structure of the anterior chamber angle, marking the peripheral termination of Descemet's membrane, so it is not the exception.

questions.title: The superior orbital fissure transmits:
questions.question: The superior orbital fissure transmits:

explanations.A: The ophthalmic artery enters the orbit through the optic canal, alongside the optic nerve, not through the superior orbital fissure.
explanations.B: The superior orbital fissure, between the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid, transmits the ophthalmic (first) division of the trigeminal nerve into the orbit, along with the oculomotor, trochlear and abducens nerves and the superior ophthalmic vein. This is distinct from the optic canal, which instead carries the optic nerve and the ophthalmic artery. Knowing which structures pass through which of these two adjacent openings matters clinically for localising lesions at the orbital apex or cavernous sinus.
explanations.C: The optic nerve passes through the optic canal, not the superior orbital fissure.
explanations.D: The central retinal artery is a branch of the ophthalmic artery that reaches the eye within the optic nerve's sheath, via the optic canal, not through the superior orbital fissure.
